intro: A polynomial is an expression built from powers of x added together, like 3x squared plus 2x minus 5. This branch covers multiplying polynomials out and, in reverse, factoring them (breaking them into pieces that multiply together), a key skill for solving equations later.

IV.6.01.what: Learning the words used to describe polynomials, such as term, coefficient (the number in front) and degree (the highest power).

levels.a: Picks out the terms, the numbers in front of each, and the plain number on its own.
levels.b: Finds the degree, the highest power of x.
levels.c: Writes a polynomial in standard order, highest power first.
levels.d: Names a polynomial by its degree and number of terms, such as "quadratic trinomial".

IV.6.02.what: Adding and subtracting polynomials by combining matching terms, like x squared with x squared.

levels.a: Adds two polynomials by combining matching terms.
levels.b: Subtracts, remembering the minus sign changes every term in the second bracket.
levels.c: Lines up matching terms in columns to add or subtract.
levels.d: Writes the perimeter of a shape whose sides are expressions.

IV.6.03.what: Multiplying a single term, like 5x cubed, across a bracket of several terms.

levels.a: Multiplies a number across a bracket.
levels.b: Multiplies a term with letters and powers across a bracket, adding the powers.
levels.c: Handles a negative term in front, changing every sign inside.
levels.d: Writes the area of a rectangle whose sides are expressions.
levels.e: Finds the missing term that was multiplied across a bracket.
levels.f: Uses a known equation to evaluate a bigger expression without finding x.

IV.6.04.what: Multiplying two brackets with two terms each, like (x + 2) times (x + 8).

levels.a: Uses a box diagram to multiply two brackets.
levels.b: Multiplies every term in one bracket by every term in the other.
levels.c: Does the same when there are numbers in front of the x.
levels.d: Does the same with negative signs.

IV.6.05.what: Recognizing special products, patterns like (a + b) squared, that can be multiplied out quickly.

levels.a: Squares a sum, like (x + 8) squared, using the pattern.
levels.b: Squares a difference, like (x minus 8) squared.
levels.c: Multiplies a sum by a difference, like (x minus 8)(x + 8), where the middle terms cancel.
levels.d: Uses the patterns for mental math, such as working out 93 squared.
levels.e: Treats a group of terms as a single block to use a pattern.
levels.f: Chains patterns together, such as going from x plus one over x to its fourth powers.

IV.6.06.what: Multiplying longer polynomials, where each bracket may have three or more terms.

levels.a: Multiplies a two-term bracket by a three-term bracket.
levels.b: Organizes the multiplying in a box diagram.
levels.d: Checks a claimed answer by trying a number for x on both sides.
levels.e: Finds one chosen term of the answer without multiplying everything out.
levels.f: Finds hidden numbers in the brackets from terms of the answer.

IV.6.07.what: Factoring out the greatest common factor: the biggest piece every term shares.

levels.a: Finds the largest factor shared by several terms.
levels.b: Takes it out in front of a bracket.
levels.c: Takes out a negative factor so the bracket starts with a positive term.
levels.d: Takes out a shared bracket, like (x + 6), as the common factor.

IV.6.08.what: Factoring by grouping: splitting four terms into pairs, factoring each pair, then pulling out the bracket they share.

levels.a: Splits four terms into two sensible pairs.
levels.c: Pulls out the bracket the two pairs share.
levels.d: Regroups the terms differently when the first grouping gets stuck.
levels.e: Groups three terms against one instead of two pairs.
levels.f: Uses grouping to crack an equation and find all its solutions.

IV.6.09.what: Factoring expressions like x squared minus x minus 42 into two brackets, by finding two numbers that multiply and add correctly.

levels.a: Finds two numbers with a given product and a given sum.
levels.b: Works out whether those numbers are positive or negative.
levels.d: Checks the factoring by multiplying the brackets back out.

IV.6.10.what: Factoring squared expressions that have a number other than 1 in front of the x squared.

levels.a: Multiplies the first and last numbers, then finds two numbers with that product and the right sum.
levels.b: Splits the middle term into two parts using those numbers.
levels.c: Factors the four terms by grouping.
levels.d: Uses guess and check as another route, testing the middle term.

IV.6.11.what: Factoring a difference of two squares, such as x squared minus 49, into (x minus 7)(x + 7).

levels.a: Recognizes when an expression is one square minus another.
levels.b: Factors it into a minus bracket and a plus bracket.
levels.c: Does the same with numbers in front, like 64x squared minus 49.
levels.d: Keeps factoring when a piece is again a difference of squares.
levels.e: Factors when one of the squares is a whole bracket.
levels.f: Uses the pattern to count whole-number solutions of a puzzle.

IV.6.12.what: Factoring perfect square trinomials, three-term expressions that are really one bracket squared.

levels.a: Recognizes the pattern of a perfect square.
levels.b: Factors it into a bracket squared.
levels.c: Does the same with numbers in front of the x.
levels.d: Chooses the last number to make an expression a perfect square.

IV.6.13.what: Factoring a sum or difference of two cubes, such as x cubed plus 216, using a set pattern.

levels.a: Recognizes numbers and terms that are perfect cubes.
levels.b: Factors a sum of two cubes using the pattern.
levels.c: Factors a difference of two cubes.
levels.d: Uses a memory trick for getting the signs right.

IV.6.14.what: Factoring completely: using every tool in turn until no piece can be broken down further.

levels.a: Takes out the common factor first.
levels.b: Chooses which pattern fits what is left.
levels.c: Keeps going until every piece is fully factored.
levels.d: Recognizes expressions that cannot be factored with whole numbers.
levels.e: Works through three rounds of factoring.
levels.f: Adds and subtracts a clever term to turn an expression into a difference of squares.

IV.6.15.what: Dividing one polynomial by another, much like long division with numbers.

levels.a: Divides each term by a single term.
levels.b: Uses long division to divide by a bracket like x + 5.
levels.c: Uses synthetic division, a quick shorthand for dividing by x plus or minus a number.
levels.d: Writes the answer as quotient and remainder.
levels.e: Divides by harder brackets, or finds a missing number to make it divide evenly.
levels.f: Finds missing numbers so one polynomial divides another exactly, without full division.

IV.6.16.what: Working with identities: equations that are true for every value of x, and using them as tools.

levels.a: Checks whether an equation is true for every x by expanding both sides.
levels.b: Checks a famous identity with real numbers.
levels.c: Uses that identity to generate whole-number right-triangle sides, like 5, 12, 13.
levels.d: Uses identities for mental math, such as 82 squared minus 68 squared.
levels.e: Rewrites a polynomial in powers of a bracket like x + 3.
levels.f: Uses an identity to do a big calculation with almost no arithmetic.
